Positions Available: Pastrycook
Location: Darwin, Northern Territory
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $567,510–$75,000

ABOUT US
Skills and Hands NT Pty Ltd is a Northern Territory-based consultancy focused on workforce planning, talent engagement, and sustainable staffing strategies. We work alongside local businesses to support the development of strong, reliable teams through tailored pathways that align with their long-term goals. Our role is to facilitate practical workforce solutions that help employers attract and retain skilled talent—contributing to the resilience and continuity of operations across the Territory.

ABOUT THE EMPLOYER
We are supporting a hospitality group (SXW Pty Ltd) based in Darwin that operates across several popular venues, specialising in Aussie-Italian and Aussie-Filipino fusion cuisine. The business is known for it's commitment to handcrafted meals, warm service, and consistent customer satisfaction. They are currently hiring for the following role: Pastrycook. These roles offer a great opportunity to join a dynamic team and grow within a stable, fast-paced hospitality environment.

PASTRYCOOK
Job Overview:
The Pastrycook is responsible for baking and decorating pastries, cakes, and desserts that align with our menu and visual presentation standards.

Key Responsibilities:
Prepare and bake a range of desserts, tarts, and cakes.
Decorate and plate desserts attractively and consistently.
Maintain cleanliness and food safety in the pastry section.
Assist in developing and testing new recipes.

Requirements:
Certificate III in Patisserie or Commercial Cookery or equivalent.
Previous pastry/baking experience in a commercial kitchen.
Creativity, precision, and understanding of HACCP.

EMPLOYEE BENEFITS
Competitive salary starting at $67,510 (with scope to increase based on experience)
Opportunities for internal advancement and skills training
Positive, inclusive work environment

HOW TO APPLY
We are looking for professionals who are passionate about hospitality and can demonstrate their experience clearly and confidently.

To apply, submit the following:
Resume outlining your work experience and references.
A short cover letter (max. 300 words) explaining:
Why you are applying for this position; and
An example of when you showed excellent service, initiative, or teamwork (use the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result).
A Written Response (max. 600 words) describing how your skills and experience align with the responsibilities of the role you are applying for. Please structure your example(s) using the STAR method.

Only complete applications that address all three components will be considered. Incomplete or generic submissions will not be shortlisted.

If you are interested in joining a vibrant team and contributing to a high-quality hospitality experience, we look forward to receiving your application.

Apply online only. Walk-in applications will not be accepted.

Position: Cook
Type: Full-time
Employer: P and S Brothers Pty Ltd trading as Spill the Beans at Palm Beach Jetty
Location: Rockingham WA 6168
Salary: $80,000 p/a
About the Business:
Spill the Beans at Palm Beach Jetty is a popular coastal café located on Rockingham’s beautiful Esplanade, right opposite the jetty. We specialise in all-day breakfast, cooked-to-order lunches, freshly baked cakes and high-quality WA-roasted coffee, all served in a relaxed, family-friendly and dog-friendly environment with stunning ocean views. Our café focuses on consistent quality, friendly counter service and creating a welcoming atmosphere where locals and visitors can enjoy delicious food in a laid-back seaside setting.
About the Position:
The Cook plays a central role in delivering high-quality, consistent meals that meet the expectations of our busy coastal café. Working as part of a small kitchen team, you will prepare a range of breakfast and lunch dishes to order, maintain food standards and support the smooth daily operation of the kitchen so that every customer receives fresh, well-presented food in a timely manner.
Key Responsibilities:
Prepare and cook a wide range of café-style breakfast and lunch dishes to order in accordance with recipes, portion sizes and presentation standards
Maintain high standards of food quality, consistency and hygiene throughout service
Manage mise en place, stock rotation and basic inventory control to minimise waste
Follow all food safety, hygiene and workplace health and safety procedures
Clean and maintain kitchen equipment, workstations and storage areas to the required standard
Assist with menu preparation, specials and seasonal dish development as required
Work collaboratively with front-of-house staff to ensure efficient service and accurate order fulfilment
Support kitchen opening and closing procedures
Requirements:
Australian citizens and permanent residents are encouraged to apply
Certificate IV in Commercial Cookery, or Diploma / Advanced Diploma in Hospitality Management
Minimum of 1 year relevant experience as a Cook
Strong practical cooking skills suited to a busy café environment, good time management, attention to detail, and the ability to work effectively under pressure while maintaining food quality and hygiene standards
Reliable, flexible and team-oriented approach with clear communication skills
How to Apply:
To apply, applicants must submit their resume with a valid email address through this online portal.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Paralegal | Brisbane CBD  
  Immediate Start available  
  3-Month Full Time Temporary Position (Potential for Extension)  
  $60 + per hour depending on experience  
  An exciting opportunity is currently available for a detail-oriented and motivated Paralegal for an immediate start to join a dedicated team located in Brisbane. This is a full-time, temporary position working within a leading native title service provider.  
  If you are a legal support professional who enjoys working across interdisciplinary teams and has a passion for supporting traditional owners to pursue their native title rights, this is the role for you.  
  You will assist in the delivery of a comprehensive and holistic legal service under the guidance of a qualified legal practitioner and direction of the Deputy Principal Lawyer. You will support traditional owners and Prescribed Bodies Corporate across the Southern and Western Queensland region. Your daily responsibilities will include:  
 
  Legal Documentation & Research:   Performing research on case law and claim groups, as well as assisting with the preparation of legal documents, affidavits, applications, legal submissions, and briefs.  
  Court & Administrative Support:   Filing and servicing court documents, delivering and retrieving briefs to/from Barristers' chambers, performing transcription duties, and taking meeting minutes.  
  Stakeholder Liaison & Communication:   Drafting correspondence and newsletters, assisting with meeting preparations, and attending workshops and seminars.  
  Project & Risk Management:   Collaborating with Client Management Teams (CMT) to assist with client management plans, monitor risks, and provide regular updates on matter activities.  
  Systems Management:   Managing records according to information management standards, ensuring currency on project tracking platforms, and actively maintaining internal legal databases.  
 
  We are looking for an organised, self-motivated professional with a collaborative approach to legal administration. To be successful, you will possess:  
 
  Technical Expertise:   Proficiency on a Windows platform, Microsoft Office suite, and experience with database and workflow management tools.  
  Industry Background:   Previous experience in a paralegal role is desirable, along with a demonstrated knowledge of the cultural, political, economic, environmental, and social issues affecting First Nations people.  
  Communication Style:   Sound oral and written communication skills, an excellent telephone manner, and the ability to build effective relationships across multidisciplinary teams.  
  Resilience & Capabilities:   Exceptional organisational skills, high attention to detail, a current open driver's licence, and the ability to undertake regular travel throughout Queensland and work occasional weekends as needed.  
 
  Please apply via the link or reach out to Martenique Crawford for a confidential chat via email at martenique.crawford@randstad.com.au  

 At Randstad, we are passionate about providing equal employment opportunities and embracing diversity to the benefit of all. We actively encourage applications from any background.

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Remuneration: $72.41 - $81.68 per hour + Salary packaging + Superannuation 
Employment Type: Permanent Part Time
Position Classification: Clinical Nurse Consultant Grade 1
Hours Per Week: 8 hours per week 
Requisition ID: REQ672868
Located in: Tamworth Hospital 

Application close date: Wednesday 5th August 2026 

Supporting people to live well, right through to the care that matters most.

This is a unique opportunity to combine your nephrology and palliative care expertise in a specialist role supporting people living with advanced kidney disease across hospital, community and home settings. As the Renal Supportive Care Clinical Nurse Consultant, you will provide expert care, symptom management and compassionate guidance-helping patients and families make informed choices and receive care aligned with their values and goals.

Every conversation, every visit and every decision you make has the potential to make a lasting difference.

Be Part of Something Bigger

Join a supportive multidisciplinary team of nephrologists, nurses and allied health professionals dedicated to improving the lives of people living with kidney disease across the New England and North West region.

Based at Tamworth Hospital, you'll provide specialist renal supportive care through home visits, hospital consultations and collaborative partnerships with community and palliative care services. You'll also work alongside the John Hunter Hospital Renal Hub to improve symptom management for people with advanced kidney disease while contributing to innovative models of care and service improvement.
Enjoy the autonomy to lead your practice with the support of an experienced team that values collaboration, professional growth and exceptional patient care.

Grow Your Career While Changing Lives

We're looking for an experienced Registered Nurse who combines advanced clinical knowledge with empathy, leadership and a passion for person-centred care.

You will bring:

Current AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse.

At least five years' post-registration experience in nephrology and-or palliative care.

Postgraduate qualifications in renal or palliative care, or a willingness to undertake further study.

Strong clinical assessment, communication and care coordination skills.

Experience working collaboratively across hospital and community settings.

A commitment to person-centred, evidence-based care and continuous improvement.

A current NSW Driver Licence and willingness to travel across the region.

What we can offer: 

At Hunter New England Local Health District, we are committed to supporting our people to succeed.

You will benefit from:

A comprehensive and structured induction program.

Ongoing professional development through face-to-face and online learning opportunities.

The opportunity to develop specialist expertise in a unique and evolving area of healthcare.

Exposure to a broad network of healthcare professionals and services across NSW.

A supportive and collaborative multidisciplinary team environment.

A positive team culture that values connection, celebrates achievements and supports wellbeing.

If you're passionate about delivering compassionate, person-centred care and want to help shape the future of renal supportive care, we'd love to hear from you.

Need more information? 
Click here for the Position Description
Find out more about applying for this position. For role related queries or questions contact Tracey Boonstra on Tracey.Boonstra@health.nsw.gov.au

Additional Information: 

Hunter New England Health is dedicated to fostering a child-safe environment that respects and upholds the rights of children and young people, aligned with NSW Health's commitment to implementing the Child Safe Standards. We aim to ensure that children and young people feel safe, supported, and included in their care. All current and prospective staff are expected to prioritise the safety, welfare, and well-being of children and young people, actively working to protect them from harm and abuse.

At Hunter New England Local Health District, we are an inclusive employer dedicated to fostering a diverse, inclusive, and welcoming workplace. Our commitment to a workforce that reflects the community we care for is essential for delivering the highest quality healthcare to our community. We encourage people with diverse lived experiences to apply. If you require any accommodations or adjustments to the recruitment process, please let us know when you apply or at any stage of the process. We will work with you to meet your needs and create the best possible experience. Please contact HNELHD-Diversity@health.nsw.gov.au for confidential support.

To be eligible for permanent employment in this position you must be an Australian Citizen, or a permanent resident of Australia, or a New Zealand citizen with a current New Zealand Passport. Employment of a temporary visa holder may only occur if no suitable local candidate is identified for the position; in this instance, you may only be offered employment in line with the conditions and expiry date of your visa.

We are unable to accommodate visa sponsorship for applicants requiring a visa for this position. 

Job share - part-time arrangements will be considered.

Applicants will be assessed against the essential requirements and selection criteria contained within the position description (link below). For assistance addressing selection criteria visit: https:--bit.ly-3vL5fq2
